 Live Trump Asia trip live updates: Trump joins Philippine president for bilateral meeting 
 Trump will participate this week in a trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi. 
 1:46 President Donald Trump and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. inspect an honor guard during an arrival ceremony at Malacanang Palace in Manila, Philippines, November 18, 2026. Carlos Barria/Reuters By ABC NEWS Last Updated: November 18, 2026, 2:24 AM EST Share President Donald Trump is traveling to Asia for meetings with global leaders and for his second visit to China for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
 See the most recent developments below.
 Key Headlines
 1 hour and 47 minutes ago Trump announces new trade agreement with Philippines 
 12:06 AM EST Trump previews US cooperation on energy, defense in meeting with Philippine president in Manila 
 Nov 17, 2026, 10:59 PM EST Trump greeted by Philippines’ president at Malacanang Palace 
 Nov 17, 2026, 8:22 AM EST Trump signs trade 'statement' with Thailand, says deal will be finalized in 'coming weeks' 
 Here's how the news is developing. 1 hour and 47 minutes ago 
 Trump announces new trade agreement with Philippines 
 President Donald Trump announced a new trade agreement between the U.S. and the Philippines in Manila on Wednesday, describing it only as a "very big trade deal" without elaborating on the details of the agreement.
 The White House did not immediately respond to a request for additional information. Trump indicated that the agreement was unexpected.
 President Donald Trump and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. speak during a welcome ceremony at Malacanang Presidential Palace, November 18, 2026, in Manila, Philippines. Win McNamee/Getty Images "We've just consummated a very big trade deal, the biggest trade deal we've ever made, by far, And it's a fair deal for both countries, and we're very happy with that," Trump said during the luncheon following a bilateral meeting with Filipino President Ferdinand Marcos.
 "And we didn't know that that was going to take place, but it took place very quickly. And it's a magnificent deal for both," Trump said.
 -ABC News' Nicholas Kerr, Michelle Stoddart, Fritz Farrow and Meghan Mistry 
 12:06 AM EST 
 Trump previews US cooperation on energy, defense in meeting with Philippine president in Manila 
 President Trump arrived at the palace of Philippine President Marcos for a bilateral meeting. Marcos warmly welcomed Trump, but also repeatedly noted how short Trump's visit to the summit is. 
 President Donald Trump sits next to Secretary of State Marco Rubio during a meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at Malacanang Palace in Manila, Philippines, November 18, 2026. Carlos Barria/Reuters 
 "The United States is our only treaty ally, and our relationship has continued to grow and evolve over the many years," Marcos said. "Now we are also exploring new areas of cooperation, particularly in technology, where American leadership and innovation continues to lead the way."
 Marcos pointed specifically to artificial intelligence as one of the ways that the Philippines can work more closely with the U.S. 
 President Donald Trump meets with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., right, at the Malacanang Presidential Palace in Manila, Philippines, Nov. 18, 2026. Mark Schiefelbein/AP Photo 
 Trump was flanked by some of his top aides, including newly-tapped Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. 
 The president pointed to a few key areas of cooperation, including energy and touted U.S. defense support for the Philippines that the leaders would build on during the visit. 
 President Donald Trump and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. shake hands at Malacanang Presidential Palace on November 18, 2026, in Manila, Philippines. Win McNamee/Getty Images 
 "The United States is now the world's leading producer of oil and natural gas by a lot, and we've just announced a major new pipeline in Alaska to export affordable, abundant supplies of energy to our allies and friends across the Pacific. And the Philippines would be a very natural partner in this effort. We're working on that," Trump said.
 Trump, who has long focused on his own renovation projects on the White House, praised the Philippine president's residence. 
 "We've been there together for a long time. Our people share common history, common values, common interests, common architectural tastes. I love what you've done here. You've done a fantastic job,” Trump said.
 Nov 17, 2026, 10:59 PM EST 
 Trump greeted by Philippines’ president at Malacanang Palace 
 President Donald Trump was greeted by Philippine President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Wednesday local time, when the two men met at the historic Malacanang Palace in Manila.
 The pair shook hands, exchanged greetings and then walked a short distance before the country’s two national anthems played, alongside a 21-gun salute as the sound of the artillery went off behind them.
 President Donald Trump and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. inspect an honor guard during an arrival ceremony at Malacanang Palace in Manila, Philippines, November 18, 2026. Carlos Barria/Reuters Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Trade Rep. Jamieson Greer and Dan Scavino stood nearby on the red carpet throughout the ceremony. The administration officials then shook hands with Marcos.
 President Donald Trump inspects honor guards during an arrival ceremony at Malacanang Palace in Manila, Philippines, November 18, 2026. Eloisa Lopez/Reuters Cameras captured the two leaders entering the Palace, where President Marcos gave him a brief tour showing him the painting, “The Blood Compact,” which sits prominently at the top of the palace’s Grand Staircase. Marcos also showed several Christmas trees positioned near the painting.
 President Donald Trump and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. speak during a welcome ceremony at Malacanang Presidential Palace, November 18, 2026, in Manila, Philippines. Win McNamee/Getty Images Trump then signed a photo book and turned it around to showcase his message: “This is such a great honor – the U.S.A. loves you!”
 President Donald Trump and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. shake hands at Malacanang Presidential Palace on November 18, 2026, in Manila, Philippines. Win McNamee/Getty Images -ABC News' Nicholas Kerr 
 Nov 17, 2026, 8:22 AM EST 
 Trump signs trade 'statement' with Thailand, says deal will be finalized in 'coming weeks' 
 President Donald Trump and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul signed a joint trade statement on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit in Manila, the Philippines, on Tuesday, saying the formal agreement will be finalized "in the coming weeks."
 "It's a joint statement agreement between United States of America, the Kingdom of Thailand, on reciprocal trade. It's a very big, actually, it's a very big trade deal," Trump said, after he was asked about the document he signed, given that a formal trade deal has not yet been reached.
 Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and President Donald Trump take part in a signing of a US-Thailand trade agreement at the Solaire Resort on the sidelines of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila on Nov. 17, 2026. Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images "And I look forward to finalizing the details of our formal agreement in the coming weeks," Trump said earlier. "Our staff is working on it very diligently, and it'll be done. But the concept of what we have will be really very permanent, and we're just about there."
 The Thai prime minister also pointed out that there is "still more" work to do, but said he is confident an agreement would be reached "soon."
 "I believe the agreement will bring greater dynamics to our trade relations and open new opportunities for all stakeholders," Charnvirakul said. "Mr. President, your leadership in bringing this negotiation to a nice conclusion like this is greatly appreciated. Yet there is still a little more to do. I'm confident that the agreement will be ready for us to sign real soon."
 Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and US President Donald Trump shake hands after taking part in a signing of a U.S.-Thailand trade agreement at the Solaire Resort on the sidelines of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila on Nov. 17, 2026. Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images According to Trump, Thailand will eliminate all tariffs on U.S. exports under the deal, in addition to removing "substantial non-tariff barriers on American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry" and purchasing $2.6 billion in U.S. agricultural products.
 Trump said this deal "lays the foundation for much stronger trading relationship that will bring the United States and Thailand closer than ever before," adding that the countries’ current ties are "the closest we’ve ever been."
 -ABC News' Emily Chang
